top3.headline: OpenAI cuts API prices in half with GPT-6.1 Terra
top3.whyItMatters: Agent tasks just got cheaper, so rerun your cost model before signing longer vendor commitments.

top3.headline: Cursor releases the framework behind its own reviewer and security agents
top3.whyItMatters: A Cursor team built a PR reviewer in about a day; decide who owns custom agents.

top3.headline: OpenAI claims AI-produced proofs on three major math and physics problems
top3.whyItMatters: Outside experts will verify them; if they hold, AI's research value moves from claim to proof.

items.title: Cursor adds DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at under $1 per task
items.takeaway: Cursor says every effort level sits on its CursorBench cost frontier, at $0.60 to $0.98 per task.
items.soWhat: Cursor says no model scores higher at these costs, though the benchmark is Cursor's own.

items.title: Anthropic's S-1 flags power and natural gas as cost risks
items.takeaway: The Verge reports some planned Anthropic data centers rely on on-site natural gas turbines.
items.soWhat: Energy supply is now a named risk to AI vendor costs; factor it into long contracts.

items.title: OpenAI says its models proved results on ETH and Yang-Mills
items.takeaway: Claims include an ETH refutation and a Yang-Mills existence proof; outside expert groups will verify.
items.soWhat: If experts confirm them, AI becomes a research partner; until then treat these as OpenAI's claims.

items.title: Cursor opens the SDK it uses to build its own agents
items.takeaway: Agents are code: Markdown prompts, TypeScript tools, built-in evals; deploy to Cursor or self-host.
items.soWhat: Teams can now build review and security agents on the same framework a major vendor runs.

items.title: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra halves API prices for agent work
items.takeaway: $1 per million input tokens, $5 output; OpenAI says Sol and Astra stay better for the hardest coding.
items.soWhat: Cheaper computer-use models make more agent workflows worth running; recheck which tasks now pay off.

items.title: Anthropic ships a Claude plugin built with about 30 nonprofits
items.takeaway: Skills and connectors for fundraising, marketing and hiring, plus deeper discounts and a two-person Team minimum.
items.soWhat: Most nonprofit users have under 10 seats, so Anthropic is courting small teams with discounts and kits.

items.title: Nvidia pitches factory-built AI data centers to Europe
items.takeaway: Huang pointed to DSX POD: Vera Rubin modules built, cabled and tested before delivery.
items.soWhat: Prebuilt, pretested AI factories aim to cut the time from order to working compute.

voices.quote: Competition for access to electrical supply and data center locations with adequate power availability is intense.

hotOnX.text: GPT-6.1 Terra: a fast, lower-cost model for computer use, visual reasoning and writing, at 50% lower API prices.
hotOnX.note: A big price cut on a model built for agent work changes many cost plans.

hotOnX.text: Claude for Nonprofits: a plugin of skills and connectors built with about 30 nonprofits.
hotOnX.note: Deep discounts and ready-made kits put Claude within reach of very small teams.

hotOnX.text: Cursor's Agent SDK: the framework behind Bugbot and Security Reviewer, now open for building your own agents.
hotOnX.note: Builders get the same agent toolkit a major coding vendor uses internally.

hotOnX.text: Europe is building its AI ecosystem, from AI factories to agents to robots; DSX POD ships factories ready to produce.
hotOnX.note: Europe's AI build-out is a recurring theme, and Nvidia wants to supply it.

hotOnX.text: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is now in Cursor, on the CursorBench cost frontier at $0.60 to $0.98 per task.
hotOnX.note: Developers watch for cheap models that still code well.
